authorization.rationale: Baseline 2.0.0 left May and December as the shallowest months of the year (16.5% and 11.7% of the grid below three contributions). Measurement showed the shoulder months need only a looser scene cloud filter, not a widened registry, so the fix costs no reproducibility at all.

problem_record.note: January remains the shallowest month at 0.215 and is unchanged by this amendment; deepening it further would require a looser wet-season filter and is a separate owner decision.

measured_alternatives_for_the_shoulder_m.why: recovers most of the depth with no reproducibility cost, because every admitted product stays on the Collection-1 lineage

measured_alternatives_for_the_shoulder_m.option: widen the registry, scene cloud filter 40
measured_alternatives_for_the_shoulder_m.rejected_because: buys a few points of depth at the price of the Collection-1 lineage and its reproducibility, which the shoulder months do not need

measured_alternatives_for_the_shoulder_m.option: widen the registry, scene cloud filter 60
measured_alternatives_for_the_shoulder_m.rejected_because: same reproducibility cost as above for a further fraction of a point

why_not_the_remaining_dry_months: Months 6 to 11 already sit at 0.0% below three contributions, so a looser filter would buy them nothing while taking on the measured EVI2 cloud bias. They keep the accepted filter of 40.

regimes.reproducibility_note: admits pre-Collection-1 products that ESA has not yet reprocessed and is actively reprocessing; unchanged by this amendment
regimes.retirement_condition: the wet-season months of the accepted source years are fully available on the Collection-1 lineage

regimes.reproducibility_note: every admitted product is on the Collection-1 lineage; this regime differs from the dry season only by its scene cloud filter, and carries no reproducibility compromise
unchanged from amendment v1 except that May and December moved to the shoulder regime

cloud_filter_basis.shared_with: the wet-season regime, which uses the same value
cloud_filter_basis.why_not_looser: The same measured EVI2 cloud bias applies: no systematic contamination was found in NDMI or NBR, but EVI2 carries a positive offset growing with cloud, +0.027 at 40-60% and +0.043 at 60-80% against a clean dispersion of 0.087. Sixty takes the depth while holding that bias at its smaller value.
cloud_filter_basis.test_limits: the leakage test covered 12-25% of the extent in January and 74.5% in March, spanned two months, and did not fully separate contamination from the correlation between cloud and rainfall

science_bindings_unchanged.statistics: monthly median and population standard deviation over datatake composites
